from.place: The higher derived functors of an exact functor followed by a left-exact functor are the derived functors of the latter evaluated after the exact functor.

title: Derived functors after an exact functor
statement: Let $\mathcal A,\mathcal B,\mathcal C$ be abelian categories, and suppose $\mathcal A$ and $\mathcal B$ have enough injectives. Let $T:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ be exact and suppose that $T(I)$ is $U$-acyclic for every injective $I$ of $\mathcal A$, where $U:\mathcal B\to\mathcal C$ is left exact. Using the right-derived-functor convention of [def-sp-left-exact-additive], for every object $M$ of $\mathcal A$ and every $i\geq0$, the $i$-th right derived functor of $U\circ T$ at $M$ is canonically isomorphic to the $i$-th right derived functor of $U$ evaluated at $T(M)$. The notions of abelian category, injective resolution, and acyclicity are those of [def-sp-abelian], [def-sp-injective-resolutions], and [def-sp-acyclic].

proof.text: Choose the Mathlib injective resolutions I₀ of M and J₀ of T(M) [def-sp-injective-resolutions]. For any injective resolution I of M, construct its mapped augmentation single₀(T(M)) → T(I) using singleMapHomologicalComplex and T.mapHomologicalComplex.map I.ι. Exactness of T preserves homology, so this augmentation is a quasi-isomorphism. Construct φ₀ : T(I₀) → J₀ by InjectiveResolution.descOfQuasiIso over the identity; it is a quasi-isomorphism.

source.place: Lemma 015M (derived-lemma-compose-derived-functors), proof: choose an injective resolution and apply the first functor

proof.text: The hypothesis hTU makes every term of T(I₀) U-acyclic [def-sp-acyclic], and the terms of J₀ are U-acyclic because they are injective. Apply Functor.quasiIso_map_of_rightAcyclic_nat from [lemma-weil-pbc-leray-acyclicity] to φ₀. Thus U(φ₀) is a quasi-isomorphism and its degree-i homology map is an isomorphism.

source.place: Lemma 015M (derived-lemma-compose-derived-functors), proof, final appeal to Lemma 015E (derived-lemma-leray-acyclicity)

proof.text: Use InjectiveResolution.isoRightDerivedObj [def-sp-left-exact-additive] for I₀ and J₀, the complex-composition isomorphism, and the homology isomorphism of Step 2 to construct e. For arbitrary I, J and a lift φ, use injective-resolution desc maps α : I₀ → I and β : J₀ → J [def-sp-injective-resolutions]. The maps φ₀ ≫ β and T(α) ≫ φ agree on the mapped augmentation. The proved private helper homotopy_of_resolution constructs a homotopy between them by coinduction, using exactness of the source and injectivity of the target terms, as in Mathlib InjectiveResolution.descHomotopyZero. Apply U to the homotopy and take homology. Combine the resulting equality with the naturality of isoRightDerivedObj at α and β and the naturality of mapHomologicalComplexCompIso at α. Reassociating these compositions yields exactly the required formula for e.hom for every I, J and φ.

lean.statement: theorem exists_rightDerived_exact_comp_iso {A : Type u₁} {B : Type u₂} {C : Type u₃} [Category.{v₁} A] [Category.{v₂} B] [Category.{v₃} C] [Abelian A] [Abelian B] [Abelian C] [EnoughInjectives A] [EnoughInjectives B] (T : A ⥤ B) (U : B ⥤ C) [T.Additive] [PreservesFiniteLimits T] [PreservesFiniteColimits T] [U.Additive] [PreservesFiniteLimits U] (hTU : ∀ (I : A), Injective I → U.rightAcyclic (T.obj I)) (M : A) (i : ℕ) : ∃ e : ((T ⋙ U).rightDerived i).obj M ≅ (U.rightDerived i).obj (T.obj M), ∀ (I : InjectiveResolution M) (J : InjectiveResolution (T.obj M)) (φ : (T.mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℕ)).obj I.cocomplex ⟶ J.cocomplex), T.map (I.ι.f 0) ≫ φ.f 0 = J.ι.f 0 → e.hom = (I.isoRightDerivedObj (T ⋙ U) i).hom ≫ HomologicalComplex.homologyMap ((mapHomologicalComplexCompIso (Iso.refl (T ⋙ U)) (ComplexShape.up ℕ)).inv.app I.cocomplex) i ≫ HomologicalComplex.homologyMap ((U.mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℕ)).map φ) i ≫ (J.isoRightDerivedObj U i).inv
